To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 3D Moving Elements Method (MEM) track model is developed to replace the Timo-shenko beam considered in the earlier studies, adopting the Eulerian coordinates and a modal approach to reduce the number and the computational cost of the model.
the proposed 3D moving element method is able to describe the high-frequency dynamics of the wheelset-track system, which was not possible using the Timoshenko beams in previous models.
A new 3D track modelling approach based on the Moving Elements Method is presented to extend the frequency range of the train-track interaction models to high frequency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a 3D Moving Elements Method (MEM) for modelling the track, which is suitable to describe high-frequency dynamic phenomena.
the study of high frequency dynamics of railway vehicle-track interaction.
the development of a 3D model of the track based on the Moving Elements Method (MEM) and its use in the study of the wheel-rails interaction in the high frequency domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MEM track model permits to extend the frequency range of the train-track interaction model up to 4 kHz for the vertical and up to 1 kHz for the lateral direction, and that the results are very close to the ones provided by the Timoshenko beams.

the proposed 3D track modelling approach is able to describe the high-frequency dynamics of the train-track system, and therefore it can be applied to study the high-frequency phenomena related to the wheel-rail rolling contact.

, in the high-frequency regime, the 3D MEM model is able to describe more precisely the track dynamics than the Timoshenko model, and that it permits to extend the range of validity to frequencies above 2 kHz.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed 3D moving element method (MEM) track model is a suitable approach to describe the high-frequency dynamics of the wheel-rails contact.

the 3D Moving element method (MEM) is proposed to model the track, the model considers an Eulerien coordinate system attached to a moving vehicle, the resulting formulation permits to significantly reduce the computational cost and the model is suitable to model high frequency dynamics.
we have proposed a 3D Moving Finite Element Method (MEM), which is an Eulerian coordinate model, to simulate the track in the high frequency range of the vehicle dynamics, which is above the 1,5 kHz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed 3D Moving-Element Method is suitable to describe high-frequency dynamics of the wheel-rails system.
the MEM is an accurate and efficient tool for modelling the track in the high frequency domain.

the MEM approach can be applied in a wide range of problems related with the train-track interaction, such as the wheel-rail contact force, the wheel-rail creep forces or the dynamic behaviour of the vehicle and the track.
